title: Lester slap-tongues Louis Jordan out of the contest in Greenville, Mississippi
summary: Lester played the same lines slap-tongued, which Jordan could not match on soprano.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Anyway, you were talking about this cutting session with Louis Jordan and Lester Young. "Running Wild" and playing the Blues...

The Blues and another one they played. "Yes sir, that's my baby..." Those were about the two tunes they played. Les blowed so much horn on that thing, and Louis Jordan was running over that soprano... You know, the soprano is more piercing than the alto. So they got to running over that. So Les said, "The only way I'm gonna get him, I'm gonna slap-tongue him." Les could slap-tongue, and play the same thing slap-tonguing than he played ordinarily, which I never heard nobody do it but him. So that's why everybody turned around and said, "Man, this man here has got it." You know what I mean? But Louis was gettin' over that horn just like he was at that time. You know what I mean? Of course, Les went away from him like that as far playing the horn. Louis played all right, but he couldn't play no horn like Les. That was in Greenville, Mississippi.
